articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition by BiLSTM Recurrent Neural Networks and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In the last years of this decade, the recognition of human activity has become important to a wide range of researchers in pattern recognition and human-computer interaction as a result of its wide range of real-world applications, such as gesture recognition, biometric user identification, surveillance by authorities, behavior analysis and health monitoring of the elderly. Human Activity Recognition (HAR) has become a significant topic in mobile and ubiquitous computing as a result of the widespread use of wearable sensor devices and the Internet of Things (loT). Deep Learning (DL) is one of the most commonly used problem-solving techniques in the HAR system. Nevertheless, there are major challenges in applying HAR to problems in recognizing various human activities. In this paper, presented and showed the activities of implementing a new combination of DL methods for multi-class user activity identification to HAR. Using DL methods can be extracting discriminative features automatically from raw sensor data. Specifically, in this work, we proposed a hybrid architecture that features a combination of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BILSTM) networks and support vector Machines (SVM) for the HAR task. The UCI HAR dataset is used to test the model, it consists of accelerometer and gyroscope data obtained from smartphones. The dataset is split into 30 % for testing and 70% for training. The results for the (BILSTM-SVM) model, showed that the highest accuracy for all users was 98.74 %, higher than all previous models using the same dataset.

articleTitle: Automated Classification of Skin Lesions Using Different Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Human skin cancer is the most common death. Skin cancer is defined as the abnormal growth of skin cells that most commonly occurs in areas of the body that are exposed to sunlight, but it can occur anywhere on the body. In their early stages, the majority of skin cancers are curable. As a result, detecting skin cancer early and quickly can save a patient's life. The incidence of malignant melanoma, the most dangerous type of skin cancer, rises year after year. Detecting skin cancer from a skin lesion is difficult due to artifacts, low contrast, mole, scar, etc. Due to the new technological advancements, early detection of skin cancer is now possible. This paper uses K-nearest neigbour (KNN), Artificial neural network (ANN) and support vector machine (SVM) classifiers for segmented and non-segmented groups and shows 95.8% overall accuracy for all classes, with the sensitivity of 97%, 91.4% and 99.7% for Benign, melanoma, seborrheic keratosis, respectively as well a precision of 92.4%, 96.6% and 99.7%, respectively. With all automatically extracted features, the accuracy is better in a non-segmented case. This paper could be extended and further processed to meet an everyday demand of how the lesions are classified or if there are any cancers.

articleTitle: Enactment of KNN in Brain Tumor Recognition: A Censorious Explication
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The accurate study of a brain tumor's morphology is truly a challenging process, and as a result, a computerized method for tumor detection is currently still being used. Unquestionably, this is more efficient than surveillance study and produces findings that are more reliable. The suggested strategy is innovative for both tumor identification and the capacity to determine the percentage of total brain cells that the tumor occupies. Brain tumors are characterized by the collection of aberrant cells in particular brain tissues. The patient's medication and prognosis are greatly influenced by the patient's past differentiating evidence of brain tumors. Finding and analyzing a brain tumor is frequently a difficult and time-consuming task. In this study, we have introduced a knowledge-based MRI brain tumor detection method for efficient categorization and grading of brain tumor images. Pre-screening, edge detection, identification, and fragmentation are the four components that make up the proposed framework. It is initially necessary to remove any noise from the source images using the Median Filter since noise could affect how accurately the identification process works. The images are instantly converted into three-dimensional blocks.

articleTitle: Automated Heart Diseases Detection Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: An extensive number of people might be affected by heart disease (HD), a major health issue that can occur anywhere in the world. Therefore, early diagnosis of cardiac disease is advantageous for treatment. A technology that can easily diagnose heart disease must be developed because the number of people with the condition is rising quickly. In addition, the patient's smoking history affects whether a problem is present or not. The HD system can define the most crucial cardiovascular patient characteristics and identify high-risk patients, but it can also model these characteristics to make it simple and clear to distinguish between them. Age, chest discomfort, blood pressure (BP), gender, cholesterol, and heartbeat are a few examples of factors that are taken into account while applying and comparing machine learning algorithms. The major goal of this article is to create a fundamental machine learning model to enhance accurate cardiac disease diagnosis. In our study, we used a HD dataset to construct a machine-learning-based diagnosis method for heart disease prediction (Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN), Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)). To evaluate the performance of classifiers, we employed cross-validation, feature selection techniques, and well-known machine learning metrics like classification accuracy, specificity, and sensitivity. The suggested system makes it simple to distinguish between those who have cardiac disease and those who are healthy. Additionally, each classifier's receiver optimistic curves and area under the curves were calculated. All of the classifiers, feature selection algorithms, preprocessing techniques, validation techniques, and metrics for measuring the performance of the classifiers utilized in this study have been covered. A smaller collection of features and the complete set of features have both been used to validate the performance of the suggested system.

articleTitle: Determine The Levels of Importance of Units In The Reliability Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In this paper we will studied the following problems i.How to calculate the reliability for the complex system used in this paper? ii.How to find the importance of each component in the complex system? For question (i), we will study two methods for evaluating the reliability of a complex system, namely the pivotal decomposition method which depend on the component selection of the complex system, and the sum-of-Disjoint-products (SDP) method. As for the question (ii), the importance of each component present in the structure of the complex system was calculated according to the Birnbaum measure (single derivative), and thus we will find the level of each component and its impact on the system. Where importance is considered one of the methods to improve the reliability systems in general. This is done to determine the location of the concentration of compounds to achieve the maximum benefit from the improvement efforts.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine for Advance Treatment: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: A machine being used to simulate cognition with the smallest degree of human participation is known as artificial intellect (AI). Many people think that the invention of machines marked the start of machine learning. The Czech word “robota,” referring describes bio artificial tools used for indentured servitude, is where the term “robot” originates. The quickly growing field of surgical care, which retains the surname of the artist Leonardo Da Vinci and therefore is utilised for challenging urologic and gynecologist surgeries, is Leonardo Da Vinci's lasting contribution to this field. The robot designs in Da Vinci's art books served as the starting point for this innovation. AI commonly referred to as computer vision, was first formally added in 1956. The expression is able to describe a variety of medical ideas, encompassing human physiology, automation, clinical issue, and now even modern “omics”, The main applications of artificial intelligence in healthcare focus of this evaluation conceptual as well as practical. The virtualized branch includes informatics methods for proactive medical therapy judgement, data augmentation information assurance, and administration of patient care system, especially electronic medical records. The best example of the brick and mortar location is a robot that assists an old client or a physician in the operating room. Customized nano technologies, a cutting-edge pharmaceutical delivery technology, are another subset of this discipline.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Multi-Target Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks via Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Multiple target detection and energy efficiency are the biggest challenges in wireless sensor networks (WSN). In this paper, we propose a compressed sensing (CS) approach for multi-target detection. The proposed algorithm uses the time of arrival (TOA) to find the number and location of targets. This approach reduces the number of bits sent and reduces the number of transmission processes over the network (the sensor sends information of all targets in one pack to the cluster head (CH)). This extends the lifetime of the limited-energy sensors in the network. The results, obtained via Monte Carlo simulations, show that the proposed approach presents substantial energy reduction without compromising target detection accuracy for a relatively large number of targets.

articleTitle: Review: Adaptive Mobile Learning Algorithms Current State-of-the-Art
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Adaptive mobile learning algorithms offer a promising approach to addressing the challenges of mobile learning, such as learner engagement and personalized learning. Recent advances and innovations in these algorithms have shown promising results in improving learning outcomes and user satisfaction. However, there are still several limitations and challenges to overcome, including the need for standard evaluation metrics, large-scale data and computational resources, and addressing ethical and privacy concerns. Future research should focus on developing effective and efficient adaptive mobile learning algorithms that can optimize the learning experience for all learners. To review and compare the current state-of-the-art adaptive mobile learning algorithms, we conducted a systematic literature review following the PRISMA guidelines. We searched multiple academic databases, including IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and ScienceDirect, using specific keywords related to adaptive mobile learning algorithms. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, we selected a total of 10 studies published between 2017 and 2021 for our analysis as in table 2, and studies that were published before the year 2010 as in table 1. We extracted data from each study, including the research design, sample size, algorithm used, evaluation metrics, and results. We then synthesized the data and identified common themes and patterns across the studies.

articleTitle: Design Methodology of Inductive Power Links for Implantable Medical Devices Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Power Links (IPL) have been extensively researched in recent decades to enhance and optimize Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) for implantable medical device (IMD) applications, providing a safe alternative to conventional batteries. Significant advancements in manufacturing have enabled wireless implantable devices to overcome size limitations that were previously a challenge. This paper aims to present a literature review of the works conducted by researchers in wireless inductive power transmission for powering Implantable Medical Devices (IMDs). The paper will discuss the design methodology, techniques, challenges, and limitations related to this technology. In addition, the paper will comprehensively examine and analyze performance-related parameters, including operating distance, Power Transmission Efficiency (PTE), and volume. This analysis will provide a comparison that can serve as a valuable resource for researchers in this field.

articleTitle: Image Steganography Based on Pixel Topology and Threshold on Selected Pixels Differences
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In this paper, the author has suggested a steganography technique that exploits pixels topology with a pre-determined embedding threshold that uses RGB (Red, Green, Blue) values of the cover image, changes them to binary and uses the least significant bit (LSB) method of replacement for twenty four bit colored image to embed the confidential image's RGB bits in the cover-image's RGB bits. The method used in embedding and extracting the secret image is novel and will be discussed thoroughly in the paper, and the quality metric used was the Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR) to measure the difference in the cover before and after embedding the secret image. Experimental results denote impressive PSNR db values where the stego image in terms of visual is indistinguishable from the original, and the secret image extracted from the stego-image is identical copy of the original embedded secret image with 100-db PSNR.

articleTitle: Roles and Challenge of Social Media in E-Commerce Through Expert Review
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Everyone and every business has been profoundly impacted by social media to the point where it can no longer be ignored. Its growth has been meteoric in every market around the globe. E-commerce sites' ability to facilitate social interaction between vendors and buyers is becoming increasingly important in the framework of the current digital revolution. The most popular type of app was social media, followed by games, shopping, and messaging. The primary objective is to provide a comprehensive overview of the research conducted on a particular topic. It also can establish context for a research topic by demonstrating how current research builds on past work. This paper has searched pertinent literature using databases such as Google Scholar, PubMed, Scopus, etc. They employ particular keywords and criteria to identify the most pertinent articles. The identified papers undergo a screening based on their titles and abstracts. The most relevant results are chosen for full-text viewing. The text emphasizes the significance of social media in the evolution of e-commerce and the need for businesses to adapt and utilize these platforms for successful consumer engagement, brand development, and overall growth.

articleTitle: Study of Machine Learning for Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Gestural input is starting to get more attention in today's technological landscape. The primary objective of this research is to create mathematical algorithms for HCI that can recognize human movements. The limited forms of human- computer interaction that now exist include the keyboard, mouse, touch screens, and a few more. While all of these gadgets have the potential to make computers more adaptable, they are limited in several ways. Among these methods is gesture detection, which may be used to create more intuitive interfaces for the average person. Hand and facial movements are common places to begin gesturing, although gestures may originate from wherever the body is moved or altered. Users may control the devices with just their gestures, eliminating the need for physical contact. Motions like page turning and vertical/horizontal scrolling need specific hand movements that are the focus of this research.

articleTitle: Image Enhancement Using HSV Color Space, DWT, and BiHE Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Image enhancement is vital in computer vision and image processing applications. This study introduces an innovative approach combining HSV color space, Discrete Wavelet Transforms (DWT), and Bi Histogram Equalization (BiHE) techniques. By converting the image from RGB to HSV, we separate color and intensity information, allowing us to enhance the intensity component for improved visual quality. The DWT is then applied to decompose the image into frequency sub bands, enabling targeted manipulation of specific frequency components to enhance image details and overall appearance. Additionally, the BiHE technique enhances contrast while preserving local image details. The proposed method was evaluated on various images, including tissue, football, Lena, and yellow lily. The results show that the proposed method achieved high Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) values, with tissue achieving 32.1853 dB, football achieving 30.5452 dB, Lena achieving 27.1462 dB, and yellow lily achieving 25.2015 dB. The Mean Squared Error (MSE) values were also low, with tissue having an MSE of 0.0006, football having an MSE of 0.0009, Lena having an MSE of 0.0022, and yellow lily having an MSE of 0.0031. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in enhancing the visual quality, details, and contrast of the images while maintaining naturalness and avoiding artifacts. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional techniques, significantly enhancing visual quality, details, and contrast while maintaining naturalness and avoiding artifacts.

articleTitle: Heart Arrhythmia Classification Using Deep Learning: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Heart arrhythmia is an irregular heartbeat that causes heart problems. It can be classified by their seriousness into serious and non-serious arrhythmia. Mainly to diagnose heart arrhythmias, we use Electrocardiogram (ECG). In this paper, the authors compared three different models of classifiers: Convolutional Neural Network, Dense Neural Network and Long Short-Term Memory to classify cardiac arrhythmia into two types normal and abnormal, using the MIT-BIH database. The results show that CNN and DNN have the best result of the models with 99% accuracy while LSTM shows 60 accuracy percent.

articleTitle: A Safeguard and Safety in E-Health Records: A Committed Clinch
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Mobile healthcare and medical services have become quite popular thanks to an influx of medical gadgets and enhanced usability of remote health services. The patient’ accessible interest with their own care and their accessible moral outrage over it combine with these. As a result, a tone of medical data is produced. These data sets need to be transferred, archived, and accessed securely. Through the use of a very effective encryption system, we have suggested a practical method for maintaining the identity and safeguarding the privacy of clinical data in this study. We have also talked about an authorization framework that makes use of different levels of access. Various entities frequently have access to medical records with differing levels of authorization. We have also talked about an authorisation framework that makes use of different levels of access. Various entities frequently have access to medical records with differing levels of authorization. In this study, we managed the access control mechanism of patient data according to the AI scheme. The framework for access control is created using the ML access model. The main justification for utilising this architecture is the ML-based restriction on accessing the data through AI. Additionally, for the proper data access regulation, the encryption of medical data utilising a variety of authorisation approaches has become necessary. It could affect user confidence in the e-health paradigm and, as a result, improve usability on a large scale.

articleTitle: Avoidance of Scalability Problem in Recommendation System Using Filtering Approch
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: By evaluating and applying some filtering to identify the user's interests, the recommendation system operates on the principle of proposing or recommending things, products, books, movies, etc. Users need to be recommended with products related to their areas of interest in order to maximize business growth and profit-gain. The recommendation system has been put in place to satisfy this need. In this study, the topic of discussion is the recommendation system and how various concepts might function both separately and jointly to make recommendations. The emphasis of this investigation is on e-commerce method recommendations. The “scalability” is a factor in the circumstance. Studies on scalability have also been conducted, and an effective solution to somewhat lessen these issues has been identified. In order to accomplish that goal, “LCW Aspect” is going to implement and analyze the user's culture, weather, and local scarcity while concentrating on resolving the problem of recommendations for new and emerging users.

articleTitle: Modernizing The Shopping Experience: The Smart Shopping Cart
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The holiday season brings out the crowds at shopping centers in major cities. When there are substantial savings to be obtained, this becomes even more true. People today often fill their shopping carts with a wide selection of products. Once a customer has finished shopping, he or she should head to the counter to settle the payment. It takes time for the cashier to create the bill using a barcode scanner. Because of this, there are often substantial wait times at the cash registers. This project proposes a solution for retail centers to address the issues mentioned above. This might be accomplished by installing RFID tags on all mall merchandise and retrofitting all shopping carts with a radio-frequency identification reader and a liquid crystal display. Any item placed in the shopping cart will have its barcode scanned automatically, and the trolley's digital signboard will update to show the item's name and price. When an item is removed from a shopping cart, its cost is subtracted from the grand total, and the relevant data is transmitted to the central billing unit through radio-frequency (RF) modules. Customers may save a ton of time since billing can be done right on the tram. The researchers worked on developing a shopping cart, which is smart, and this system allows for faster checkout and payment of the bill in a secure manner, and the adoption of technology in the store increases the demand for it continuously, the computer will remember the barcode data you enter and compare it to its database, from which it will get the necessary data. The database and RF model will be connected through software. Small radio-frequency (RF) electrical modules called a “transmitter” and “receiver” can be used to transmit and receive signals between any two devices. The data is sent from the transmitter module to the receiver module, which then processes the data. The group believes that the intelligent shopping cart will result in a more dependable checkout procedure and less waiting time for customers.

articleTitle: IoT System of Medical Equipment Monitoring and Ambulance Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: With the rapid development in the field of information and communication technology, taking advantage of this development has become an urgent necessity in most areas such as the military, engineering, agriculture, and health life. The developers have provided an appropriate environment that accommodates most of these areas, which take on responsibility for looking for speed of implementation, speed of access, remote management, and other features that are in high demand and need. This paper introduces one of the important applications in the field of the Internet of Things (IoT) that is related to human life and health. a smart ambulance system implemented. Patient data collected by sensors are distributed in an ambulance and continuously received at the hospital side based on cloud computing, then it is sent to the specialists to give decisions, that may help to save critical cases according to the received information and it may need quick access and intervention by them Access to the patient shortens the time, especially during peak times. The ambulance tracking is done through the navigation monitoring system.

articleTitle: Implementation of High Gain DC/DC Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In order to bypass the ordinary DC/DC boost converter and level up the DC voltage to a higher level, the high gain boost converter is described in this work. With just one semiconductor switch unit, the circuit can level up a little DC voltage to a huge level of DC voltage. In order to prevent the system from becoming saturated, a typical DC/DC boost converter will restrict the boosting production at a specific level. The suggested topology introduces the integration between the high switching state and the transformer, producing a larger output voltage. The PSIM program is used to run the simulation, and a hardware lab scale setup is used to experimentally validate it. The desired output voltage is 200V, which will be generated by a modest 48V DC system. Additionally, the effectiveness of the overshoot study converter and the regular boost converter is compared in this study.

articleTitle: AI-based Applied Science for Detection of Land Suitability in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: According to a report conducted by the Food and Agriculture Organization, the world population is projected to increase by another two billion people by the year 2050, but the arable land is only predicted to increase by 5%. Therefore, to increase agriculture productivity, clever and effective farming methods are required. One of the key instruments for the growth of agriculture is the assessment of agricultural land suitability. In order to collect and process agricultural information, a number of new technologies and innovations are being used in agriculture. The Internet of Things (IoT) has been empowered as a viable tool for automation and decision-making in the field of agriculture, which has sparked the construction of low-cost and compact sensor devices.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Long-Range Electrical Loads in Najaf Province Using Markov Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Economic factors, such as the cost of electricity, which includes prices, production factors, government support, and the technical conditions of the electric sector, population growth rate, gross domestic product per capita, and urban expansion regarding the electricity demand, have an impact on electricity in the province of Najaf (as is typically the case in the provinces of Iraq). Despite government and private sector efforts to invest in this field, the current rise in demand has resulted in a deficit and a widening disparity between the two forces (supply and demand). Due to their efficiency in predicting long-term behavior, Markov chains are frequently used in various industries, including labor planning, weather forecasting, and stock market analysis. The prediction approach for the electric power field has the disadvantage that Markov chains are not used. In the present work, we propose a simple predictive tool for predicting future fitted load rate, highest load rate, and lowest required load rate. Markov chain modeling is used. In this paper, the prediction feature of Markov models was presented, where a miniature model was taken using the electrical current data of Al-Najaf Governorate for the years 2018–2022. By using Markov models, it was predicted how the results could be for the following years. The transition probability matrix, initial probability Vector, and proof were all computed. Determine the mean time to return, determine that the matrix is an ergodic Markov series, and forecast long-range electrical loads using the static distribution.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dual-Way Converter Using Modified H-Bridge Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: This paper presents a modified H-bridge circuit that can operates the common converter in power electronic study namely full wave rectifier. The common topology used to drive the full wave rectifier known as Wheatstone bridge circuit to perform the conversion. However, the default H-bridge circuit has the body drain diode in the power switches which can cause a leakage current and allow the reverse current direction during the conversion. This problem can be solved by modified the default H-bridge with a different topology to block the reverse current phenomenon. This study is simulated using PSIM software and validate thru hardware implementation. The final results show the proposed circuit can handle the conversion perfectly without facing any noise or disturbance.

articleTitle: Energy Losses of Proposed Grid-Connected PV System in Iraq

abstract: This study's major objective is to apply the PV*sol premium valentin programme to conduct an analysis of the energy losses that would be incurred by a projected PV system in Iraq that would be connected to the grid. The photovoltaic (PV) system that has been proposed uses 18 polycrystalline modules, each of which has 4.68 kWp area of 30.2 square metres, with a 30-degree tilt. articleTitle: Optimization of Corona Rings Parameters for 765kV and 500kV Polymer Insulators
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In recent years, polymeric insulators have played an essential role in the power transmission system. To control the electric field strength and voltage distribution along the surface of the insulators. In this research, corona rings were used at the ends of the 765 kV and 500 kV polymeric insulators depending on the two-dimensional (2D) finite element method(FEM) and optimizing the position and dimensions of the corona rings using the Nelder Mead algorithm. The optimization problem is achieved by decreasing the electric field strength by obtaining the parameter values for optimal corona loops. According to the numerical results, the Nelder Mead technique reduced the field strength by 69% for the 765 kV insulator compared to the field strength at the original values of the corona rings and 32% of the field strength for the 500 kV insulator. This methodology is characterized by high-performance speed and can be applied to different levels of voltages.

articleTitle: Integrating Haar Wavelet Transform and Image Processing for Accurate Fire Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: We discussed the proposed methodology for fire detection, which includes six stages: data acquisition, IoT transmitter, compression, recognition, enhancement, and analysis and evaluation. The methodology was implemented using MATLAB 2021 with specific computer specifications. The study used a webcam to capture a fire image and extracted color pixels from it. The Haar wavelet transform was used to compress the image and detect the red color information. Several image enhancement techniques, such as histogram equalization, Wiener filtering, and median filtering, were used to improve the image's quality. The inverse Haar wavelet transform was used for image recognition and analysis. This methodology can be useful for detecting fires in real-time and can be further improved with more advanced techniques.

articleTitle: Distributed Cache Performance Improvement Middleware Session
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Smart gadgets are increasingly providing in-demand services, and speedier access to important services is crucial. By using the Internet and telecommunications operators' expanded bandwidth, billions of smart sensors, motors, automobiles, devices, mobile phones, tablets, and people communicate in a distributed environment to obtain on-demand service. This work created a session and cookie middleware and used DHT server polymorphism to increase proxy server distributed cache efficiency for automotive services. Node clustering makes peers function as client/servers, listening to the TCP Port line and using cookie-session middleware to provide services. If there is only one node, a client/server will listen to the UDP port and use the DHT protocol to register peer properties. Game theory-based architecture is also suggested in this study. Weak Sequential Equilibrium (WSE), an extensive-form game with partial data, has been found to contain Nash and weak sequential equilibriums in one state. The simulation findings show that the suggested architecture is faster than constructing a virtual cache and moving from busy nodes, decreasing user response and bandwidth usage and increasing cache hit rate.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Training Board for Basic Gates Using Switches, Diodes, Transistors, and Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: the paper deals with designing and constructing a realistic educational and training board that is non-consumable, durable, high quality, and enjoyable to work on with the trainees. The contemporary world is witnessing these days “rapid” progress in the field of electronic technology, especially digital ones. The developments that took place in the areas of computer applications and the Internet in providing computer applications through simulation that contribute to the delivery of information and increase the understanding of learners. as well as through video films that are shown via the Internet and YouTube applications, so it is necessary to think about setting goals and strategies to raise individual differences between Learners and ensure that they are achieved to understand and assimilate the scientific material. articleTitle: Nucleus Detection Using Deep Learning Approach on Pap Smear Images
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Cervical cancer is caused by the abnormal growth of female cervix cells. It is one of the most familiar factors for women”s death worldwide. Therefore., early detection of cervical cancer leads to a reduced mortality rate and increased chance of being alive. The Papanicolaou is a common method for screening and identifying the cancerous cells in a woman”s cervix. The resultant pap smear images may help the physician diagnose the cervix cells. The crucial part of the cell is the nucleus. Therefore., auto-detection of the nucleus is the core point in this paper. A deep learning algorithm is employed to segment the nucleus in pap smear images. Two network structures., known as ResNet18 and ResNet50., are exploited to detect the nucleus part in the cell. The results are compared with ground truth and between the two structures. Both networks., ResNet18 and ResNet50., perform almost the same., with test accuracy reaching 92%. This work distinguishes it from other work in simplicity., fast., and accuracy. Therefore., it can be recommended to be used in clinical units and rural countries which suffer from the lack of specialist physician.

articleTitle: Digital Predistorter Model for High Power Amplifier For Nonlinearity Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Nonlinearity is a major problem in High Power Amplifier (HP A), which results due to the limited physical structure of the HP A manufacturing design. This limitation effects the transmitted signal in amplitude and Phase. This paper address this challenge via designing a digital predistorter (DPD) model which can handle the mentioned challenge. The proposed DPD model estimates (predicted) the reverse error to deals with the nonlinearity effect. The results of the simulated model present a superior performance over other methods, a comparisons via different metrics is presentd.

articleTitle: Solving Bi-Objective Reliability Optimization Problem of Mixed System by Firefly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The main objective of reliability optimization of a particular system, such as a mixed or complex system, is to determine the best way to obtain an increase in the final reliability of this system by allocating high reliability to the important components of the system. In this paper, the problem of optimization reliability of the mixed system is studied using the firefly algorithm based on two cost functions, which are the logarithmic function and the exponential function. Some modifications have been made to these two functions to suit the reliability system under study, where very good results have been obtained for the overall reliability of the mixed system at a reasonable cost. Also, it was found that the overall system reliability is directly proportional to the total cost.

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Characterization Supercapacitor using Constant Current Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Supercapacitors are high-energy electrochemical capacitors with high power density, long cycling life, fast charge-discharge response, and greater capacitance. In this paper, a new result using voltage measurement full charging for supercapacitors using the constant current charging method is presented. The detailed test procedure for 188 farads of supercapacitors manufactured by Eaton was observed in the laboratory to develop a dynamic model of a supercapacitor under a constant charging current of 6A. The model includes R-C branches built with a consideration of linear and nonlinear factors, variation temperature and effects of leakage current. The experiment was conducted with simple laboratory equipment like a constant current supply, voltage data logger and computer. The computational time required for the parameter calculation is by applying parameter identification modelling techniques tools in MATLAB/Simulink. Results were verified by analysis of comparison experimental with a simulation of the derived equivalent circuit. The longest respond time charging during the 42 V.

articleTitle: A Proposed Cryptography Key Management in Software-Defined Networking (SDN)
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Software-defined networks (SDNs) separate the control and data planes, consolidating control functions in a central entity called the controller. However, this dynamic nature poses new challenges, specifically the inability to secure the network and the need for secure communication between network devices without impacting network speed and performance. Cryptography key management is essential to network security, but traditional methods are often complex and difficult to manage in SDN environments. This paper proposes a key management scheme to achieve secure distribution of RSA certificate keys, which can then be used to encrypt data sent over the network. We propose a new approach to cryptography key management in SDN with an approach that prevents unauthorised access to these keys using a physical Mac address. It is designed to be more flexible, scalable, and secure. The proposed approach is based on using a hierarchical key management system that allows administrators to manage keys for different network devices and applications easily. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, we conducted a series of experiments using a testbed implementation of an SDN network. The results show that the proposed approach effectively manages cryptography keys in SDN environments while providing strong security guarantees and maintaining high performance. Overall, the proposed cryptography key management approach represents a significant step forward in securing SDN networks and has the potential to be widely adopted in the future.

articleTitle: EOG Based Eye Movements and Blinks Classification Using Irisgram and CNN-SVM Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The classification of eye movements and blinks is an important task in various fields, including ophthalmology, psychology, and human-computer interaction. In recent years, the use of EOG signals and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has shown promising results in accurately classifying different types of eye movements and blinks. The Irisgram, which is a two-dimensional representation of the short-time Fourier transform in the shape of a human iris, has been used as a feature for distinguishing between different types of eye movements and blinks. Additionally, CNNs have been utilized to learn the features automatically from Irisgrams and classify the eye movements and blinks based on these learned features. In this paper, we provide a methodology to classify blinks and four eye movements by employing Irisgram as input to the CNN-SVM classifier which achieved test accuracy of 96.2% in the testing dataset.

articleTitle: Automatic Vehicle License Plate Recognition Using Lightweight Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems rely heavily on automatic vehicle license plate recognition (AVLPR). This system is required for traffic control, electronic toll collection, and access to parking lots. Due to the complexity and structure of license plate design for each country, especially in Arabic countries, license plate recognition is one of the most difficult recognition problems. Using image processing and deep learning (DL) techniques, the proposed AVLPR system is applied to new Iraqi license plates (LPs). We proposed a Lightweight Convolution Neural Network (LWCNN) in this study. It has four convolutional blocks, each with a batch of Max-pooling and Dropout layers, as well as a Flatten layer and two Dense layers. This architecture is simple, fast, and dependable, with promising classification accuracy that could propel the field forward. The proposed algorithm achieved 98% detection accuracy for the standard new PLs style and 85% training accuracy for digits dataset.

articleTitle: InfraRed Spectroscopy Monitoring in Agri-Food 4.0 with Remote Sensing Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: IoT generates enormous quantities of streaming data, also known as “big data,” which opens up new opportunities for monitoring the food and agriculture industries. Big data from social media is also important for the food industry, in additional to devices. In this article, we provide a description of big data, AI, and IoT, as well as how these three technologies are reshaping the way agri-food systems are created. After a brief introduction towards the areas of IoT, big data, and AI, the role of cloud computing and big data assessment in agriculture, distribution network industrialization, social networks (for innovation process and sentimental analysis) in packaged foods, and good food appraisal (using spectral methods) are protected. Agriculture involves drone-based crop photography, intelligent farm equipment, and food security, followed by data fusion and sensor systems (using gene sequencing). Particular focus is placed on the financial potential of technologies and the findings of translational research.

articleTitle: Methodology for the Design and Programming Methods for a Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The concept of a “smart home” is important because each homeowner has his own vision and needs. The article discusses the stages of implementing the “smart home” system, conducts a comparative analysis of wired and wireless systems, and determines the main requirements of the owners of the system. It also touches on opportunities such as improving lighting, home security, remote management using mobile devices, and reducing the cost of home maintenance. The problem of omission by designers to calculate the electrical loads has a significant impact on the reliability and accuracy of the design. Therefore, we suggest looking at the loads, collecting them, and determining which of them requires operation throughout the day on two systems according to their importance and required operating hours by analyzing the loads consumed by the residents of the “smart home” and automating most of the processes, allowing you to save money, ensure safety, and increase comfort.

articleTitle: Improving the Transferring the Files in Cloud by Using Vogel's Approximation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Cloud computing is a technology that allows for the virtual integration and deployment of computing resources at remote locations. various users on the World Wide Web request various files spread on many servers across the world, which consumes time and increases the cost of sending the information under cloud computing. Reducing the time it takes to download a file is the same as lowering the cost of product delivery. The shortest amount of time necessary to provide a product to a client at the lowest attainable cost. The system's basic idea selects which server assists in delivering the file promptly to the client seeking this file. The suggested system reduces the time necessary to download the material by picking the best server that delivers the file in the lowest amount of time and is an efficient approach. VAM is used to determine the lowest cost for each file to be provided to the user inside the middle server processing client requests, as well as to specify the server from which each client would download the content. In this study, we use a variety of optimization approaches to increase query performance by reducing the time transferring the file using Vogel's Approximation Method (VAM) and the proposed system consists of three parts which are the cloud computing part, server part, and client part and used three files which is (File1, File2, File3) with (6.5, 2, 1.3) GB respectively. The results showed that the VAM contributed to reducing the cost of file transferring

articleTitle: Image Dataset for Cervical Cell Diagnosis – a Review
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Cervical cancer is a prevalent and fatal disease that affects women all over the world. This affects roughly 0.5 million women annually and kills over 0.3 million people. Recently, a significant amount of literature has emerged around the advancement of technologies for identifying cervical cancer cells in women. Previously, diagnosing cervical cancer was done manually, which could lead to false positives or negatives. The best way of interpreting Pap smear images and automatically diagnose cervical cancer are still up for debate among the researchers. Thus, as to encourage talented researchers in this field, an excellent, easily access and expert's validated data for cervical cell has been developed by previous researchers. In this study, datasets have been reviewed from previous studies that can be access for research and study purposes.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Micro Silica as Modifiers in Stone Mastic Asphalt Mixture
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Pavements might deteriorate as a result of excessive traffic and weather conditions; hence pavements must be updated to provide enhanced performance and life span. Much study has been done to assess the appropriateness of various materials for pavement alteration. The goal of this study was to improve a Stone Mastic Asphalt Mixture by using an asphalt binder that has been modified with micro-silica particles. The following parameters were used: shear mixer, revaluation speeds (2000 rpm), and time for mixing (30 minutes). To investigate the mechanical characteristics of SMA based on Marshall stability and flow, indirect tensile strength, and Cantabria abrasion loss, three micro-silica concentrations of 2%, 4%, and 6% by weight of asphalt cement were applied. The results show that Micro Silica is an excellent modifier since it has achieved maximum stability, increased tensile strength, and decreased abrasion loss. Based on this research, the ideal is MS 6%.

articleTitle: Mobile Tourism Recommender System for Users to Get a Better Choice of Tour
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: A turn-by-turn route highlight that checks whether users have actually taken a course might be added to the system to cope with fake preferences. In order to acquire more insightful client feedback, a larger customer overview with more participants is required. Our examination was designed as a lab experiment to gather initial data straight away. For the client study, we just looked at a few initial objective mixtures while making fun of other clients and their system comments. It's crucial to do a field research with actual clients using our suggested model in real-world situations (such as when looking for a course online to work from home). This will help us better understand how effective our approach is. In this article, we developed a creative method for recommending multimodal travel routes. In a client survey with 20 participants, we evaluated the applicability of our cross-breed computation and its usability. The results show that CF, information-based, and well-liked course concepts complement one another more successfully than cutting-edge course organizer advances. Our application can give seven different elective trip options thanks to the Google Guides Programming interface.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Smart Learning with Moodle-Based Raspberry Pi 4 for University Students
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Electronic learning (E-learning) has been a popular trend in education in recent years. As the cornerstone of E-Learning., the learning management system (LMS) must be available 24/7 with strong internet connectivity, enabling students to engage in paperless learning. However, not all universities, especially those in rural areas, have reliable internet connectivity. This has become an issue for universities that lack reliable internet connectivity and an adequate computer laboratory since they are unable to offer an E-learning environment that simulates a classroom setting. Even though the majority of students and teachers have smartphones, without reliable internet connectivity, it will be challenging to establish a connection to the learning management system's remote server. In this paper, a mobile learning management system based on Raspberry Pi and MoodleBox has been developed to address the aforementioned E-learning problem. This prototype can be used locally as a server even without an internet connection to provide the most fundamental LMS features. Students can view the information locally from their smartphone or laptop after teachers submit it to this portable system. This prototype has been successfully installed in our lab, and the LMS is simultaneously accessible through Wi-Fi,

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Computing: Unraveling the Physical Properties of Brain-Inspired Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Neuromorphic computing, which aims to replicate the information processing capabilities of the human brain, has gained significant attention as a promising paradigm for developing intelligent computing systems. The physical properties and characteristics of neuromorphic systems play a critical role in their performance and functionality. In this paper, we provide an in-depth exploration of the physical properties of brain-inspired systems, unraveling the key aspects of neuromorphic computing from a physical perspective. We discuss the underlying physical principles of spiking neural networks, including their operation principles and types. We also review synaptic plasticity mechanisms and their implementations in hardware. Furthermore, we analyze various hardware implementations of neuromorphic computing, ranging from traditional CMOS-based technologies to emerging technologies such as memristors, spintronics, and photonics. We discuss the advantages and limitations of different hardware technologies for neuromorphic computing, and highlight their potential in realizing brain-inspired functionalities. Moreover, we review applications of neuromorphic computing in diverse domains, including artificial intelligence, robotics, image and speech processing, pattern recognition, and sensor networks. We provide examples and case studies showcasing the potential of brain-inspired systems in real-world scenarios. Additionally, we discuss the challenges and limitations of neuromorphic computing, such as power consumption, scalability, and hardware variability, and highlight ongoing research efforts to address these challenges. Finally, we outline future directions and research opportunities in neuromorphic computing, including potential breakthroughs and emerging trends. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the physical properties of brain-inspired systems in the context of neuromorphic computing, shedding light on the current state of research, advancements, and potential applications in this exciting field.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Parameter Estimation for the Beta Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The beta distribution is useful for modeling continuous random variables that lie Between 0 and 1, such as percentages and percentages. Beta distribution begins Many different shapes can be described by two shape parameters, and, and some statistical properties such as ordinal statistics of the beta distribution and a joint density function have also been shown. It can be challenging to estimate, hence the methods of calculating moments and maximum likelihood estimation have both been researched., although the moment method is more straightforward. We check Both methods here and their comparison is used in MATLAB through code and it was based on the initial parameters (a = 1 and b= 1.5) and for different sample sizes that started from (n = 25, 50, 100, and 200) and using simulation and iteration of 3000 and comparison between the two methods through known statistical measures as mean square error (MSE), correlation coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{R}^{\wedge}\mathbf{2})$</tex> and the total deviations (TD), so through simulation experiments, we concluded that the MLE method is the best.

articleTitle: Some Methods of Finding Minimum Paths and the Importance of Reliability for a Complex System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: This article will include three important methods for extracting minimal path sets from a complex network, and a comparison will be made between these methods to choose the best one for accessing minimal path sets. Also, this article will discuss HEWEIDY'S METHOD, which is a new and effective method for calculating the importance of each component of a complex network and its levels. This method depends entirely on the relationship between minimal path sets and minimal cut sets, and the latter we will extract from minimal path sets.

articleTitle: Effect of Coarse Plastic Waste Aggregates on the Performance of Concrete-Filled Steel Tube Columns and Their Life Cycle Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of a series of concrete mixes that contain plastic waste aggregate on the behavior of concrete-filled steel tube columns under axial load. Two groups of specimens, with a total of ten columns were prepared. Hollow steel columns and columns with concrete mix were used as reference specimens for each group. In other mixes, natural coarse aggregate was partially replaced with coarse plastic waste aggregate in ratios of (2.5-5) % and a different ratio of water cement content. Ultimate axial load capacity, ductility, and failure mode are discussed for all specimens. Besides, environmental impacts by applying the life cycle assessment methodology are discussed. The results also indicated that increasing the plastic waste aggregate ratio led to decreased ultimate axial load capacities and ductility for both square and circular columns, while decreasing the water-to-cement ratio with the same plastic waste aggregate ratio resulted in an increase in ultimate axial load. The failure mode of the square columns was local buckling, which occurred near the ends of the columns, while for the circular columns, local buckling occurred near mid-height. In general, circular columns were more ductile than square columns. The results of life cycle impact assessment promote the use of concrete-filled steel tube columns with recycled aggregate. The experimental results illustrated the feasibility of using plastic waste aggregate to partially replace coarse aggregates. concrete-filled steel tube columns concrete-filled steel tube columns. Generally, the proposed concrete-filled steel tube columns have comparable performance in some characteristics with the reference columns.

Author Keywords: recycle coarse aggregate. Life cycle assessment

articleTitle: Estimation of Camera Parameters via Gray Wolf Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In machine vision for industrial growth, camera calibration accuracy is essential. In this paper, we propose an algorithm for camera calibration that combines an enhanced version of the two-step approach with Gray Wolf Optimization algorithm (GWO). First, the two-step process is enhanced to lessen distortion's impact on camera calibration. After employing the principle of slope invariance to determine the camera's distortion parameters, we employ Zhang's calibration technique to acquire the camera's internal and exterior parameters. The above-mentioned camera parameters are then optimized using a GWO approach that combines a dynamic inertia weight and a variation idea. Finally, the proposed algorithm is subjected to a series of comparative experiments, the results of which demonstrate that it achieves higher accuracy, overcomes the problem of slipping into local optimal more effectively, and achieves faster convergence in parameter optimization.

articleTitle: Decision Making Strategy for COVID-19 Risk Minimization Using Data-Driven Model
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: During a pandemic outbreak, it is crucial to build socially resilient and sustainable communities. Data-driven solutions that account for the requirements of both exist military applications and global strategies are necessary for this task. There has been a lot of interest in the smartphone-based Digital Proximity Tracing Technology (DPTT) for reducing, confining, and tracking the ongoing COVID-19 epidemic with population acceptability insights and the effectiveness of the function. This study contrasts DPTTs with Data-Driven Epidemic Intelligence Strategies (DDEIS) to emphasize their distinctions and provide a new perspective on how to deal with them. DDEIS's core features might be used to provide a social as well as technological solution for stopping the spread of disease, protecting the public's health, and getting cities back to normal as soon as possible. The influence of human behavior is considered while weighing the benefits and drawbacks of society decision making and individual choice. The SEIR (Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered) epidemiology model offers early information on user preferences in a DPTT. The suggested model's influence on the Covid-19 dissemination dynamics is assessed, and the findings are given.

articleTitle: Supremacy of Quantum Computation in Bioscience: A Technical Review
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Beyond traditional computing, quantum computing is based on quantum phenomena like entanglement and superposition. Even though quantum computing is still developing, it has had a tremendous impact on the world of computing by opening up a brand-new dimension. To fully appreciate its potential and advantages, however, there are a number of obstacles to overcome, much like with any other idea or subject. This review explains quantum computing models and identifies some advantages and disadvantages. This systematic review's key contribution is its summary of the state-of-the-art quantum computing models used in numerous fields nowadays. Based on the literature study, it offers new classifications of quantum models and connects the findings to the four main groups of quantum computing models. Evaluation demonstrates that despite their foundation in quantum operations and circuits, the majority of the studied models are either mathematical or algorithmic. In theory, quantum computers are capable of solving some tasks tenfold faster than their classical equivalents. Although the advent of practical quantum computation has not yet occurred, it will have an impact on almost all fields of science. In this analysis, we investigate the potential impact of contemporary quantum algorithms on computational science and informatics.

articleTitle: Strengthening of Unreinforced Masonry Walls by FRP Materials Exposed to In-Plane Compression Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Bricks are commonly used in developing regions because of their low cost and ease of accessibility. Buildings built with bricks symbolize Iraq's rich history and represent its rich culture. Those walls will likely fail if in-plane loads are applied to masonry walls without reinforcement. This is particularly due to their insufficient resistance to non-concentric and concentric compression loads. The historical architecture style often relied on using masonry brick; however, brick structures pose challenges when they are exposed to in-plane loading in eccentric loading scenarios, such as in the presence of lateral loads from wind, which can create eccentric compressive forces, especially if the walls are not symmetrically located within the building footprint. Uneven settlement of a building's foundation can introduce eccentricities in the loads applied to the walls. This is particularly relevant in older buildings or structures on uneven or weak soils. During an earthquake, structures experience dynamic loads that can induce eccentric forces and moments in walls, particularly if the seismic forces are not evenly distributed across the building's height or plan. Due to the age of such a structure, some upgrading and strengthening will be necessary. Choosing a strengthening methodology that does not adversely affect the appearance and operation of a building is of paramount importance. Therefore, in recent years, FRP materials have been widely used to address these problems to improve brick masonry walls' structural performance. An FRP material is typically expensive unless applied in a specific configuration for a specific stress condition, but it has many positive characteristics concerning low weight and ease of application. A current study has evaluated the effectiveness of strengthening configurations utilizing FPR materials (CFRP and GFRP) fabricated into sheets and strips in specific orientations. To achieve the objective of this study, eight masonry brick specimens were manufactured and tested until failure occurred. All specimens in each loading condition maintained the same characteristics as the dimensions of the specimen and boundary condition. The specimens of masonry brick were identified with dimensions (813×810mm) according to British Standard BSEN 1052-1: 1999. In eccentric load conditions, the GFRP material has a more significant effect on load, particularly at the cracking stage; however, this effect is less noticeable at the ultimate loading stage. At the concentric load state, the specimens with a GFRP sheet on the entire side and with CFRP in a diagonal configuration present the most significant displacement by (262.8%); moreover, the specimen with a CFRP sheet on the entire side processes the maximum increase in compression stress with (58.8%).

articleTitle: Novel Approach to Obtain Minimum Path/Cut Sets for Complex -Series Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In this paper we discuss a new method of chasm partitioning of complex - series systems. We divided the complex system into two subsystems and studied methods for determining the minimum paths and cutoffs. Through this, we have created a link between the two subsystems and the complex system. This relationship allowed us to calculate the reliability of the complex system from the reliability of each of the two subsystems, and to infer the minimum cut in the complex system by integrating the minimum cut of the two subsystems.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Beamforming Array Antennas Based on Partial Update LMS and NLMS Adaptive Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The well-known phased array antenna (PAA) is the most common and efficient way for providing adaptive Beamforming Array Antenna (BAA), which is an array of antenna elements (N) controlled by signals with well-defined phase relations between those elements. There are many proposals aimed at reducing the need for phase shifters, however these initiatives will fail until additional active control units are introduced. Despite the fact that these problems have been researched by numerous Uniform Linear Array (ULA) researchers, Partial Update (PU) adaptive filtering has never been implemented. When increasing or decreasing the number of antennas (M) for each ULA element, such that M < N, the model suggested in this study selects or deselects the RF chain utilizing PU LMS or NPULMS update partial adaptive algorithms. The ULA simulation results show that the PU LMS and NPULMS algorithms are as effective as the full band LMS and NLMS algorithms in terms of mean square error (MSE), tracking, and estimate input signal performance, but with a faster convergence time and lower steady-state error signal level. The main beam shape of the PU algorithms is very near to that of the planned uniform array pattern, and they can also reduce interference signals by null steering. However, NPULMS outperforms the PULMS algorithm in terms of efficiency.

articleTitle: Innovative Way to Evaluate the Reliability and Importance of Complex - Series Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: In this research, we used two complex systems connected in a chain, and we divided the system into two parts, and the reliability and importance of each sub-system were calculated separately, as well as the level of importance of its components. In addition to calculating the reliability and importance of each component of the original system, using the proposed method of calculation will help us to understand and realize the mechanism of increasing the reliability of all components of the system through prior knowledge of the importance and level of each component of the partial systems, and therefore this mechanism will give a clear and simple idea of the way to find reliability And the importance of the components of the system as a whole without the need to perform complex and lengthy calculations of the original system.

articleTitle: Traffic and Energy Aware Load Balancing Routing Protocol for Multipath Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Mobile Ad hoc Networks (MANETs) is one among the wireless self-organizing network which plays an important role in promising multimedia applications and as well it maintains incredible traffic demands for ubiquitous access. As the results energy utility is highly increased so that an effective routing protocol is very essential to improve the packet delivery ratio and transmission reliability of the network. For that purpose in this research Traffic and Energy Aware Load Balancing (TEALB) Routing Protocol is proposed in MANETs. This protocol is mainly categorized into three segments they are Ad hoc On-demand Multipath Distance Vector (AOMDV) Routing Process, TEALB Routing Process, and route maintenance. Using the processes multipath transmission is effectively performed in MANE Ts with effective path adjustments according to the node mobility which helps to achieve maximum packer delivery ratio and throughput during the process of communication in the network. Network Simulator (NS2) is used to simulate the performance of the proposed TEALB-MANETs. The parameters which are used for the performance analysis are packet delivery ratio, end to end delay, routing overhead and throughput. In order to perform comparative analysis the earlier protocol which are considered are SMLB-MANETS and MCLB-MANETS. After analyzing the outcome achieved from the results it is proven that the proposed TEALB-MANETs achieves high packet delivery ratio and throughput and as well lower end to end delay and routing overhead when compared with the earlier approaches.

Author Keywords: Ad hoc On-demand Multipath Distance Vector (AOMDV)

articleTitle: Counting Non-Overlapping Abnormal Cervical Cells in Whole Slide Images
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Cervical cancer is one of the most common cancer among women globally. The Pap smear test has been widely used to detect cervical cancers according to the morphological characteristics of the cell nuclei on the micrograph. The aim of this paper is to count the non-overlapping abnormal cervical cells in whole slide images automatically by employing various image techniques. The proposed approach consists of four main steps; image enhancement, transform the extended minima, remove small pixels, and count the number of abnormal cells in the image. The proposed system used 250 cervical pap smear images where the overlap between cells is minimal. The performance of the proposed system is evaluated based on comparing the manual counting and automating counting over whole images. Therefore, the accuracy is evaluated mainly on the difference between manual and automated, and it is 92.5%. The proposed method can be used in laboratory to decrease the false positive rates in counting abnormal cells.

articleTitle: Using Markov Models And Fault Tree For Finding The Reliability Of Some Engineering Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The main focus of this study is to apply fault tree analysis to a model of an electrical chip that is frequently used in computers. The block group, sometimes referred to as the failure groups, was obtained. The relationship between the FT error tree and the RBD reliability block diagrams was also discussed in this study, and it is there that we discovered a diagram that illustrates the potential mistakes that this system may be subject to. Gaining a thorough understanding of the system is the first stage in any reliability analysis, including fault tree analysis. The system's relationship to the error tree must be well understood in these situations. Then, using a random transition matrix, we converted the fault tree diagram into a Markov model by accurately documenting each component in the system, their physical and functional connections, the typical and atypical environments they encounter, and the modes of failure of each component. We were able to obtain equations, and by utilizing Laplace transforms and the inverse of Laplace, as well as finding the system mean time to failure, we were able to determine the model's reliability and carry out maintenance on the same scheme.

articleTitle: Design and Implantation of Non-Linear Digital Predistorter for High Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Nonlinearity is a major problem to reduce energy efficiency in High Power Amplifier (HPA), which is a result due of the limited physical HPA structure manufacturing design. This limitation effects the transmitted signal in amplitude, phase as well as electricity consumption. This paper address this challenge via designing a digital predistorter (DPD) model which can handle the mentioned challenge. The proposed DPD model estimates (predicted) the reverse error to deals with the nonlinearity effect, and reduces the energy consumption of the HPA. The results of the simulated model present a superior performance over other methods, a comparisons via different metrics are presented. These results shows that the proposed DPD is adaptive for HPA in traditional systems, sustainable building, smart cities, and resilient building with smart transmission systems.

articleTitle: Design of Hyperparameter Tuned Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Prediction Model for Financial Crisis
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: Financial crisis prediction (FCP) greatly contributed to the country's economic phenomenon. Precise estimation of the number and probability of failure indicated the strength and advancement of the national economy. Generally, different methods are planned for a potential FCP. In contrast, predictive accuracy, classifier efficiency, and data legality are not optimal for practical application. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods define how an agent can only study the best action policy in a sequential decision procedure through experience. The agent policy offers him some terminal and running rewards in a given situation. In online learning, the agent learns sequentially. This paper designs a novel Hyperparameter Tuned Deep Reinforcement Learning based Prediction Model for Financial Crisis (HPTDRL-PFC) technique. The goal of the HPTDRL-PFC technique lies in the identification of financial crises. To do so, the presented HPTDRL-PFC technique primarily normalizes the input financial data into a uniform format. For the prediction process, the Bayesian deep Q-Network (BDQN) technique is applied in this work. To improve the predictive ability of the BQDN technique, the artificial hummingbird optimization (AHBO) algorithm performs the hyperparameter tuning process. The performance validation of the HPTDRL-PFC technique is tested using a financial dataset. The comparative study reported the enhanced prediction outcomes of the HPTDRL-PFC technique over other models.

articleTitle: Improved Qubit Neural Network Based Computer Aided Detection Model for COVID-19 on Chest Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Engineering Technology and its Applications (IICETA)
abstract: The significance of the advanced computation model for medical diagnoses has been gradually recognized with the growth in e-health. Specifically, in the pandemic COVID19, the advanced computational modelling role is crucial plays in understanding complex clinical data in future years. Computed tomography (CT) and Chest X-ray (CXR) images were presented for the diagnosis of COVID19. The deep learning (DL) method has proven better and more efficient in several medical imaging and computer vision applications. With the increase in the COVID outbreak, researcher workers are making use of the DL method to identify coronavirus infection. This study develops a hybrid squirrel search algorithm with improved deep learning-based detection (HSSA-IDLD) system for the diagnoses of COVID-19. The major intention of the HSSA-IDLD technique lies in the recognition and discrimination against COVID-19 in healthcare images. Initially, the medical images are processed using a contrast enhancement approach. For feature extraction, an improved EfficietNet model is utilized in this study.
